Class Session

java.lang.Object
com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.Session
Direct Known Subclasses:
MuiSyncedSession
public abstract class Session extends Object
Manages the lifetime of a server-bound screen in an offscreen Window.

Open, update, and close the session on Minecraft's main client thread. The base class coordinates queued replies, per-tick health checks, and closure through hooks supplied by the subclass.

A session is the agreement between one desktop window and one framework/server binding. The window may exist before the server reply arrives. While waiting, the session gives that reply a limited number of ticks to arrive rather than freezing the client. Subclasses must safely hand background/network results to poll() and must not mutate a window directly from a network thread. The atomic closed flag prevents duplicate teardown; it does not make the other fields or native resources thread-safe.

To receive the driver's tick maintenance, initialize the subclass fields and register the session with SessionRegistry.INSTANCE.track(this) on the client thread. The base constructor only stores the window reference. Registration also lets the public window-close API find this session; dispose() removes that registration before releasing the binding and closing the window.

    • window

      @Nonnull public final Window window()

      Returns:

    • isClosed

      public final boolean isClosed()
      Checks whether teardown has been claimed, even if resource release is ongoing.
      Returns:
      true once disposal begins; never becomes false again

    • tick

      public final void tick()
      Performs one client-thread health check, called by the driver each tick.

      First accept queued replies, then check the world/player/window, then the framework binding. If no reply is pending and the subclass permits recovery, try to recreate a lost binding. Otherwise the session waits within the timeout or closes. Exceptions from polling or health hooks propagate to the registry, which logs them. A failed recovery attempt is logged here and immediately disposes the session.

    • dispose

      public final void dispose()
      Tears down the session once: untrack, release the binding, close the window.

      Call on the client thread. Framework release failures are logged, but do not prevent attempting native window closure. A second disposal request returns immediately, including one made recursively by a close callback.

    • releaseKeepingWindow

      protected final boolean releaseKeepingWindow()
      Releases ownership without destroying the native window, for a local error screen.
      Returns:
      true if this call claimed teardown

    • poll

      protected void poll()
      Accepts safely queued network/background results on the client thread. Session's default implementation does nothing. Subclasses own the thread-safe handoff mechanism.

    • isAlive

      protected abstract boolean isAlive()
      Checks the framework's current server/client binding.
      Returns:

    • shouldHeal

      protected abstract boolean shouldHeal()
      Decides whether an unhealthy binding should be recreated when no reply is pending.
      Returns:
      true to attempt recreating the binding, false to close

    • heal

      protected abstract void heal()
      Re-establishes the framework binding in the same window. If this sends an asynchronous request, call beginAwait() to bound the wait.

    • onRelease

      protected abstract void onRelease()
      Releases framework references and performs any required server close handshake. Runs after untracking and before the final native window close attempt.

    • beginAwait

    • takeAwaiting

      protected final boolean takeAwaiting()
      Consumes the expected-reply flag so a second reply is not accepted as the first. This does not itself attach a binding or validate the arriving reply.
